title: Leading weight of a subcurve span with boundary branches
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $X\subset\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ a connected generically reduced one-dimensional closed subscheme with nondegenerate reduced support $D$. Suppose $D$ is nodal, with completed singular local rings $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $L=\mathcal O_D(1)$. Let $Y$ be a nonempty proper reduced union of irreducible components, not necessarily connected, and $Z$ its reduced complementary union. On the normalization $E$ of each component of $Z$, choose $b_E$ distinct preimages of boundary nodes between $Y$ and $Z$. Write $e_E=\deg_E L>0$ and $e_Y=\deg_YL$. Suppose for every such $E$ either $b_E\le e_E$, or $E$ maps isomorphically onto a rational normal component of degree $e_E=b_E-1$ with $b_E\ge2$. Set $b=\sum_E b_E$. For $W=\ker(k^r\to H^0(Y,L|_Y))$, give $W$ weight zero and its quotient weight one. With $s=\dim(k^r/W)$ and $a_F$ as in [lem-sfb-bounded-hilbert-weight-polynomials], one has
$$s\le h^0(Y,L|_Y),\qquad a_F\ge e_Y+\tfrac b2.$$
These are geometric weight estimates with no semistability hypothesis. The nilradical of $X$ may be nonzero at finitely many points. A rational normal curve of degree $e$ means a smooth rational curve whose embedding in its own linear span is the complete degree-$e$ embedding of $\mathbf P^1$. Component degrees below are degrees of the pulled-back hyperplane line on the smooth normalized components [def-sc-normalization, def-pc-degree-line-bundle].

proof.text: Choose a basis of $V=k^r$ whose first vectors form a basis of $W$ and whose remaining vectors have weight one. Restriction induces an injection $V/W\hookrightarrow H^0(Y,L|_Y)$: its kernel is zero by the definition of $W$. Thus $s\le h^0(Y,L|_Y)$. For all sufficiently large $m$, let $H_m=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(m))$, $h_m=\dim H_m$, and let $U_{m,j}\subset H_m$ be the span of restricted degree-$m$ monomials of weight at most $j$, $0\le j<m$. The bounded Hilbert-weight lemma supplies monomial bases for $H_m$ and $w_F(m)=a_Fm^2+O(m)$ for this zero/one flag. Its coefficient is the $a_F$ in the statement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-curve-normalization-section-defect] to $X$. Write $\widetilde D=\coprod_i E_i$, $A_i=L|_{E_i}$, $e_i=\deg A_i$, and $T_{i,m}=H^0(E_i,A_i^m)$. The map $\rho_m:H_m\to\bigoplus_iT_{i,m}$ has kernel of bounded dimension, $\dim T_{i,m}=me_i+O(1)$ and $h_m=m\sum_i e_i+O(1)$. These errors depend on $X$, never on $j$. Separate the indices into components over $Y$, components of $Z$ with $b_E\le e_E$ (call this set $I$), and the remaining components (call this set $J$), which satisfy the rational-normal exception. If both alternatives hold, put the component in $I$. The sum of the $e_i$ over $Y$ is $e_Y$ by the degree convention of the item.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-nodal-subcurve-boundary] applied to $D,Y$, each selected boundary point is a smooth branch on the complementary component and has residue field $k$. Each $w\in W$ has zero value there: it vanishes on $Y$, hence at the common point, and pullback preserves its zero value. On the smooth normalization it therefore vanishes to order at least one. Put $B_E=\sum_{p\text{ selected on }E}[p]$, of degree $b_E$. A degree-$m$ monomial of weight $t\le j<m$ has $m-t\ge m-j$ factors from $W$. It vanishes identically on $Y$, and its pullback to $E$ belongs to $H^0(E,A_E^m(-(m-j)B_E))$. This assertion is closed under linear combinations, so it holds for all of $U_{m,j}$ and uses no independence of the boundary conditions.

source.place: Section 3.2, Theorem 8 proof steps (7), (9)--(10), printed pp.14--15; agent reconstruction of the selected-boundary subcurve filtration (local PDF WANTED, online PDF read).

proof.text:
For $E\in I$, [lem-sfb-smooth-curve-section-degree-cap] gives
$$\dim H^0(E,A_E^m(-(m-j)B_E))\le me_E-b_E(m-j)+1,$$
since $me_E-b_E(m-j)=m(e_E-b_E)+jb_E\ge0$. For $E\in J$, a section in the restriction of $W$ belongs to $H^0(E,A_E(-B_E))$ of degree $e_E-b_E=-1$. The same cap gives zero, so $W$ restricts identically to zero on $E$. Every monomial of weight $j<m$ has a $W$ factor, hence all of $U_{m,j}$ restricts to zero on these components as well. The dimension of an image in a finite direct sum is at most the sum of the dimensions of its component images. Rank-nullity for $\rho_m|_{U_{m,j}}$ and the bounded kernel from step 2 now give, with one constant $C$ independent of $m,j$,
$$\dim U_{m,j}\le\sum_{E\in I}(me_E-b_E(m-j)+1)+C.$$
Subtracting this from the expression for $h_m$ in step 2, and enlarging $C$, yields
$$h_m-\dim U_{m,j}\ge me_Y+\sum_{E\in J}me_E+\sum_{E\in I}b_E(m-j)-C.$$
In particular embedded nilpotents contribute only to the bounded error before summation.

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal B$ be any degree-$m$ monomial basis of $H_m$, with weights $t_M\in\{0,\ldots,m\}$. Its members of weight at most $j$ are linearly independent inside $U_{m,j}$, so at least $h_m-\dim U_{m,j}$ of its members have weight greater than $j$. Count each monomial once for every $j=0,\ldots,t_M-1$ to obtain
$$\sum_{M\in\mathcal B}t_M=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\#\{M:t_M>j\}\ge\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(h_m-\dim U_{m,j}).$$
Insert step 4 and use $\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(m-j)=m(m+1)/2$:
$$\sum_{M\in\mathcal B}t_M\ge m^2\left(e_Y+\sum_{E\in J}e_E+\tfrac12\sum_{E\in I}b_E\right)-Cm.$$
The additional term $m\sum_{E\in I}b_E/2$ is nonnegative and was dropped. Since this holds for every monomial basis it holds for their minimum $w_F(m)$.

source.place: Section 3.2, Theorem 8 proof steps (7), (9)--(10), printed pp.14--15; agent reconstruction of the selected-boundary subcurve filtration (local PDF WANTED, online PDF read).

proof.text:
Divide the inequality of step 5 by $m^2$ and let $m\to\infty$. Step 1 gives
$$a_F\ge e_Y+\sum_{E\in J}e_E+\tfrac12\sum_{E\in I}b_E.$$
For $E\in J$, $e_E=b_E-1$ and $b_E\ge2$, hence $e_E-b_E/2=(b_E-2)/2\ge0$. Since $b=\sum_{I}b_E+\sum_{J}b_E$, this proves $a_F\ge e_Y+b/2$. Together with step 1 it proves both clauses. No step used semistability or connectedness of $Y$; components with $b_E=0$ contribute zero boundary term.

lean.note: The reduced support and subcurve are represented up to their unique closed-immersion isomorphisms; the finite component family is exhaustive and irredundant. W is the existing degree-one chartwise equation subspace, exactly the kernel of restriction. The leading coefficient is specified by the existing monomial-basis weight and its eventual quadratic error. Rational-normal means an over-k projective-line isomorphism and surjectivity of the actual ambient coordinate restriction, with the prescribed normalized hyperplane degree. Helpers only specialize canonical hyperplane pullback, normalized component degree and the chart normalization already used by the bounded-weight dependency. No semistability, linear normality, reducedness of X or connectedness of Y is assumed.
